newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-NEW EUROPEAN SEASON JUST 55 DAYS AWAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW EUROPEAN SEASON JUST 55 DAYS AWAY.

text.p: Just 55 days after the final
whistle blows to end Wednesday night's European Cup Final
between Juventus and Borussia Dortmund, Europe's top clubs will
be back in action in the newly-inaugurated preliminary round of
the next European Cup.
Next season's competition starts on July 23 with 32 teams
playing in the first leg of the preliminary round with the
second leg on July 30.
The 16 winners from that will then be joined by 16 teams
exempted from the preliminary round in a qualifying round staged
on a home-and-away basis on August 13 and 27.
The 16 winners emerging from all that will then join the
champions of Europe's eight top-ranked domestic leagues in the
Champions League which starts in September.
Those 24 teams will be drawn into six groups of four teams
on Friday, August 29.
Depending on the outcome of Wednesday's final Germany could
have three teams in the expanded 24-team Champions League. If
Borussia lose, the Turkish champions Galatasaray will enter the
Champions League automatically. If Borussia win, Galatasaray
will play in the qualifying round.
One team who will be in action in July are Glasgow Rangers,
who have just clinched the Scottish title for the ninth
successive season and who were effectively European Cup
semifinalists four seasons ago.
Rangers who have spent 50 million pounds ($81.6 million) on
rebuilding their stadium and buying new players to become a
European power, will have to battle past two preliminary rounds
before reaching next season's Champions League.
Because Scotland's official ranking in UEFA's coeffecient
lists has fallen to 19th, Rangers will play their first
competitive matches of the new season in July.
Despite their impressive domestic record, Rangers have won
only three of the 18 Champions League fixtures they have played
since 1992 and lost five of the six games they played this
season.
For the first time the runners-up in the top eight ranked
European leagues will be taking part in the expanded 24-team
competition next season, but in order to reach the group phase
or Champions League they have to come through the qualifying
round.
The champions of those top eight countries qualify directly
for the Champions League although Turkey's situation depended on
the outcome of the final.
The losing teams in the preliminary and qualifying rounds of
the competition, switch to the UEFA Cup, which, from next
season, has a one-off final for the first time.
Current ranking lists (top eight countries)
Country Champions Runners Up
Italy Juventus Parma or Inter Milan
Spain Real Madrid or Barcelona
France Monaco Paris Saint Germain
Germany Bayern Munich Bayer Leverkusen
Netherlands PSV Eindhoven Feyenoord
Portugal Porto Sporting Lisbon
England Manchester United Newcastle United
Turkey Galatasaray Besiktas or Fenerbahce
Note: If Borussia Dortmund are European champions, Turkey
loses its place in the Champions League and Galatasaray will
enter the qualifying round.
